questions.stem_md: The Congress of Vienna (1815), which drew up a settlement for Europe after the defeat of Napoleon, was hosted by

options.text_md: Otto von Bismarck
Count Camillo de Cavour
Duke Metternich, the Austrian Chancellor
Giuseppe Mazzini

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The Congress was hosted by the Austrian Chancellor, Duke Metternich.
Step 2: So (c). Bismarck and Cavour belong to the 1860s unifications; Mazzini was a revolutionary whom Metternich saw as a dangerous enemy.

questions.stem_md: Which of the following was **not** a decision of the Vienna settlement of 1815?

options.text_md: The Bourbon dynasty was restored to power in France.
The Kingdom of the Netherlands, including Belgium, was set up on France's northern border.
Austria was given control of northern Italy.
The German confederation of 39 states was dissolved.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The settlement restored the Bourbons, ringed France with buffer states such as the Kingdom of the Netherlands, and gave Austria control of northern Italy.
Step 2: The German confederation of 39 states set up under Napoleon was **left untouched**, not dissolved.
Step 3: So (d).

questions.stem_md: The main aim of the European powers that met at Vienna in 1815 was to

options.text_md: reverse the changes made in the Napoleonic era and restore the old order
spread the ideas of the French Revolution across Europe
unify the German states under Prussia
give the vote to every adult man

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Britain, Russia, Prussia and Austria had defeated Napoleon. They were conservative powers.
Step 2: Their goal was to restore the monarchies and the old order that Napoleon had overthrown, so (a).
Step 3: The other options describe liberal or nationalist goals that the conservatives opposed.

questions.stem_md: Which treaty of 1832 recognised Greece as an independent nation?

options.text_md: The Treaty of Constantinople
The Treaty of Vienna
The Treaty of Versailles
The Act of Union

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Greece's struggle against Ottoman rule began in 1821.
Step 2: The Treaty of Constantinople of 1832 recognised Greece as an independent nation, so (a).

questions.stem_md: In the 1810s a young scholar walks from village to village writing down lullabies, harvest songs and old stories, saying that the soul of the nation lives in the cottage, not in the palace. His work reflects the ideas of

options.text_md: Duke Metternich
Johann Gottfried Herder
Count Cavour
Otto von Bismarck

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The scholar believes national culture lies with ordinary people and their folk songs and tales.
Step 2: That is Herder's idea: true German culture was to be found among the common people, *das volk*. So (b).
Step 3: Metternich was a conservative statesman; Cavour and Bismarck were chief ministers who unified Italy and Germany through politics and war.

questions.stem_md: After Russian occupation, the Polish language was forced out of schools. Why did many Polish priests continue to use Polish in church gatherings and religious teaching?

options.text_md: Because the priests could not understand Russian
Because the Pope had banned the Russian language
To win the military support of Prussia
Because using Polish had become a way of resisting Russian domination

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Under Russian rule, Russian was imposed everywhere and an armed rebellion in 1831 was crushed.
Step 2: Using Polish in church kept the language alive and became a form of national resistance, so (d). Many clergy were jailed or sent to Siberia for it.
Step 3: (a)–(c) are invented reasons.

questions.stem_md: In February 1848, after the king fled Paris, the National Assembly proclaimed a Republic. Which of these did it do?

options.text_md: It restored Louis Philippe as a constitutional monarch.
It gave the vote to all adult men and women.
It granted suffrage to all adult men above 21 and guaranteed the right to work.
It closed all workshops to save money.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Food shortages and unemployment brought Parisians onto the streets and Louis Philippe fled.
Step 2: The new Republic gave suffrage to all adult males above 21, guaranteed the right to work and set up national workshops to provide jobs, so (c).
Step 3: Women were **not** given the vote (b), and the workshops were created, not closed (d).

questions.stem_md: Which statement best explains why the Frankfurt Parliament of 1848 failed to unite Germany?

options.text_md: The King of Prussia rejected the crown it offered, the aristocracy and army opposed it, and it lost the support of workers and artisans.
Napoleon's armies dissolved it by force.
It refused to draft any constitution.
Britain and Russia invaded the German states.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The Parliament drafted a constitution for a German nation with a monarch whose powers a parliament would limit, and offered the crown to Friedrich Wilhelm IV of Prussia.
Step 2: He rejected it and joined other monarchs against the assembly. The aristocracy and military grew hostile, and the middle-class assembly lost popular support because it resisted the demands of workers and artisans. Troops finally forced it to disband.
Step 3: So (a). (b) is wrong by more than 30 years; (c) and (d) are false.

questions.stem_md: Women who had taken part in the liberal movement of 1848 could attend the Frankfurt Parliament only as onlookers in the public gallery. What does this fact show most clearly?

options.text_md: Women had no interest in politics in 1848.
The liberal idea of political rights at the time was limited and left women out.
The Parliament was dominated by the aristocracy.
Women already had the vote in most German states.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Women had formed their own associations and joined meetings and demonstrations, so (a) is false.
Step 2: Yet they were denied suffrage and could only watch. This shows that liberal ideas of rights in 1848 did not extend to women, so (b).
Step 3: The Parliament was dominated by the **middle classes**, not the aristocracy (c); (d) is false.

questions.stem_md: In January 1871, who was proclaimed German Emperor in a ceremony held at Versailles?

options.text_md: Friedrich Wilhelm IV
Otto von Bismarck
William I, King of Prussia
Victor Emmanuel II

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: After Prussia's victories, the Prussian king William I was proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles in January 1871, so (c).
Step 2: Bismarck was the chief minister who planned unification, not the emperor. Friedrich Wilhelm IV had refused the crown in 1849. Victor Emmanuel II became King of Italy.

questions.stem_md: Why did Sardinia-Piedmont, rather than any other Italian state, take the lead in unifying Italy?

options.text_md: It was ruled by the Pope, who wanted a united Italy.
It was the largest state in the south of Italy.
It was under Austrian rule and used the Austrian army.
It was the only Italian state ruled by an Italian princely house.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The north (Lombardy, Venetia) was under the Austrian Habsburgs, the centre under the Pope and the south under the Bourbon kings of Spain.
Step 2: Sardinia-Piedmont alone had an Italian ruling house, so it could lead a national movement against foreign rulers; under Victor Emmanuel II and Cavour it did. So (d).
Step 3: (a) and (c) describe other states, and Piedmont was in the north-west, not the south (b).

questions.stem_md: Which statement about Count Camillo de Cavour is correct?

options.text_md: He led an army of volunteers into southern Italy in 1860.
As chief minister of Sardinia-Piedmont, he used a diplomatic alliance with France to defeat Austria in 1859.
He founded the secret society Young Italy in Marseilles.
He was proclaimed king of united Italy in 1861.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Cavour was a cautious statesman, not a revolutionary or a democrat. Through a skilful alliance with France, Sardinia-Piedmont defeated Austria in 1859.
Step 2: So (b). (a) describes Garibaldi, (c) describes Mazzini and (d) describes Victor Emmanuel II.

questions.stem_md: The Act of Union of 1707 that formed the United Kingdom of Great Britain was between

options.text_md: England and Ireland
England and Wales
England and Scotland
Scotland and Ireland

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The Act of Union (1707) joined England and Scotland into the United Kingdom of Great Britain, so (c).
Step 2: Ireland was forcibly incorporated later, in 1801.

questions.stem_md: How was the formation of the British nation-state different from the unification of Germany and Italy?

options.text_md: It was the result of a slow process spread over centuries in which the dominant English nation extended its influence over the other nations of the islands.
It was achieved through three short wars led by a chief minister.
It came about through a revolutionary uprising of volunteers.
It was decided by the Congress of Vienna in 1815.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Germany and Italy were unified in the 1860s–1871 through wars and diplomacy.
Step 2: Britain had no sudden upheaval: over a long period the English, growing in wealth and power, extended their influence over the Scots, Welsh and Irish, through the 1688 shift of power to Parliament, the Act of Union of 1707 and the incorporation of Ireland in 1801. So (a).
Step 3: (b) fits Germany, (c) fits Garibaldi's campaign in Italy, and (d) is false.

questions.stem_md: In allegorical images of Germania, the crown of oak leaves stands for

options.text_md: readiness to fight
being freed
willingness to make peace
heroism

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The German oak stands for heroism, so the crown of oak leaves means heroism: (d).
Step 2: Readiness to fight is the sword, being freed is the broken chains, and willingness to make peace is the olive branch around the sword.

questions.stem_md: A nineteenth-century coin shows a woman wearing a red cap with a tricolour cockade. Which nation does the coin most probably represent, and what is the figure called?

options.text_md: Germany — Germania
Italy — Marianne
France — Marianne
Britain — Germania

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The red cap and the tricolour cockade are symbols of liberty and the Republic in France.
Step 2: The French nation was shown as Marianne, whose image appeared on coins and stamps. So (c).
Step 3: Germania (Germany) wears a crown of oak leaves, and neither figure stood for Italy or Britain.

questions.stem_md: Why did the Balkans become the most serious source of nationalist tension in Europe after 1871?

options.text_md: Because the region had been unified under one Slav kingdom
Because ethnic variety, the break-up of the Ottoman Empire and the rivalry of the big European powers combined in one region
Because the Zollverein had been extended to the region
Because Britain wanted to colonise the region directly

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The Balkans had many Slav peoples who wanted independence, while the Ottoman Empire that ruled much of the region was weakening.
Step 2: Balkan states were jealous of one another, and Russia, Germany, England and Austro-Hungary each tried to extend their control there. These forces together made the region explosive, so (b).
Step 3: The region was never unified (a), and (c) and (d) are false.

questions.stem_md: An imagined German newspaper of the 1830s reports: "From the new year, carters will no longer stop at a customs post at every border between our states, and the many coins in our purses will give way to just two currencies." Which development does the report describe?

options.text_md: The Zollverein
The Napoleonic Code
The Congress of Vienna
The Frankfurt Parliament

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The report describes the removal of customs barriers between German states and a sharp cut in the number of currencies.
Step 2: That is what the Zollverein (1834) did: it abolished tariff barriers and reduced the number of currencies from over thirty to two. So (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** At first, French armies were welcomed as bringers of freedom in many towns of Holland and Switzerland and in cities such as Milan and Warsaw.

**Reason (R):** Napoleon's administrative changes removed many feudal burdens on peasants and restrictions on trade in the areas he conquered.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: A is true: early on, French armies were welcomed in many towns.
Step 2: R is true: the Code and reforms freed peasants from serfdom and manorial dues, removed guild restrictions and improved transport.
Step 3: These gains are the reason people first welcomed the French, so R explains A: (a). (The welcome later turned to hostility.)

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The settlement of 1815 brought the Bourbon dynasty back to power in France.

**Reason (R):** The Congress of Vienna was hosted by Otto von Bismarck of Prussia.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: A is true: the Bourbons were restored in 1815.
Step 2: R is false: the Congress was hosted by the Austrian Chancellor, Duke Metternich. Bismarck became important only in the 1860s.
Step 3: So (c).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Zollverein helped bring about the economic unification of the German states.

**Reason (R):** Prussia fought three wars, against Denmark, Austria and France, between 1864 and 1871.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: A is true: the customs union of 1834 removed tariff barriers and reduced currencies, binding the German economy together.
Step 2: R is true: Prussia fought Denmark (1864), Austria (1866) and France (1870–71).
Step 3: But the wars explain the **political** unification of 1871, not the economic effects of the Zollverein, which came decades earlier. So (b).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Frankfurt Parliament succeeded in uniting Germany as a constitutional monarchy in 1848.

**Reason (R):** The Frankfurt Parliament offered the crown of a united Germany to Friedrich Wilhelm IV, King of Prussia.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: A is false: the Parliament failed; Germany was united only in 1871 under Prussian leadership.
Step 2: R is true: it offered the crown to the King of Prussia, who rejected it.
Step 3: So (d).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** German romantics such as the Grimm brothers collected old folk tales.

**Reason (R):** Romantics believed that the true spirit of the nation lay in the culture of the common people.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: A is true: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected old folk tales and published them, seeing French domination as a threat to German culture.
Step 2: R is true, and it is the very reason they collected folk culture: to recover and spread the nation's true spirit. So (a).

questions.stem_md:
**Assertion (A):** The Greek struggle for independence drew support from many educated people in western Europe.

**Reason (R):** Greece had been part of the Ottoman Empire since the fifteenth century.

Choose the correct option.

options.text_md: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: A is true: poets and artists praised Greece and helped mobilise opinion; Lord Byron raised funds and went to fight, dying of fever in 1824.
Step 2: R is true: Greece had been under Ottoman rule since the fifteenth century.
Step 3: But the reason West Europeans backed the Greeks was their sympathy for ancient Greek culture, seen as the birthplace of European civilisation, not the length of Ottoman rule. R does not explain A, so (b).

questions.stem_md: True or false? The Civil Code of 1804 gave women the same voting rights as men.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The Code did not give anyone universal suffrage, and it placed women under the authority of their fathers and husbands.
Step 2: So the statement is false.

questions.stem_md: True or false? In May 1848 the elected representatives of the German states met as a parliament in the Church of St Paul in Frankfurt.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The Frankfurt Parliament was convened in the Church of St Paul in May 1848.
Step 2: So the statement is true.

questions.stem_md: True or false? Cavour personally led the volunteer army that marched into southern Italy in 1860.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The volunteers who entered the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in 1860 were led by Giuseppe Garibaldi.
Step 2: Cavour was the chief minister who worked through diplomacy, so the statement is false.

questions.stem_md: True or false? Many of the peoples of the Balkan region were Slavs.

options.text_md: True
False

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The Balkans (today's Romania, Bulgaria, Albania, Greece, North Macedonia, Croatia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Slovenia, Serbia and Montenegro) were home to many peoples, a large number of whom were Slavs.
Step 2: So the statement is true.

questions.stem_md: The belief that a society should keep its traditional institutions, such as the monarchy and the Church, and change only slowly, is called ___.
questions.solution_md:
Step 1: After 1815, European governments followed this philosophy: they wanted to keep monarchy, the Church, social hierarchies and property.
Step 2: The answer is conservatism.

questions.stem_md: The customs union of 1834 that abolished tariff barriers among most German states was called the ___.
questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The 1834 customs union formed under Prussian leadership was the Zollverein.
Step 2: The answer is Zollverein.

questions.stem_md: The female figure chosen to stand for the French nation, shown with a red cap, the tricolour and the cockade, was named ___.
questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The French allegory took a popular Christian name and the symbols of liberty and the Republic.
Step 2: The answer is Marianne.

questions.stem_md: Match each person with what they are remembered for.

options.text_md: Giuseppe Mazzini
Duke Metternich
Otto von Bismarck
Giuseppe Garibaldi

match_right.text_md: Chief minister of Prussia who led German unification
Led armed volunteers into southern Italy in 1860
Founded the secret society Young Italy
Hosted the Congress of Vienna in 1815

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Mazzini founded Young Italy in Marseilles (p–3).
Step 2: Metternich, the Austrian Chancellor, hosted the Congress of Vienna (q–4).
Step 3: Bismarck, Prussia's chief minister, led German unification through three wars (r–1).
Step 4: Garibaldi led volunteers into the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies in 1860 (s–2).

questions.stem_md: Match each symbol used in images of Germania with its meaning.

options.text_md: Broken chains
Breastplate with eagle
Olive branch around the sword
Rays of the rising sun

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Broken chains mean being freed (p–3).
Step 2: The breastplate with the eagle stands for the strength of the German empire (q–4).
Step 3: The olive branch around the sword shows willingness to make peace (r–1).
Step 4: The rising sun marks the beginning of a new era (s–2).

questions.stem_md: Arrange these events in the order in which they happened, earliest first.

options.text_md: The Frankfurt Parliament meets in the Church of St Paul
The Civil Code is introduced in France
The German Empire is proclaimed at Versailles
The July Revolution in France brings in a constitutional monarchy
The Treaty of Vienna restores conservative rule

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Civil Code, 1804.
Step 2: Treaty of Vienna, 1815.
Step 3: July Revolution, 1830.
Step 4: Frankfurt Parliament, 1848.
Step 5: German Empire proclaimed, January 1871.
Step 6: So the order is b, e, d, a, c.

marking_scheme.step: Correct order b, e, d, a, c

questions.stem_md: Put these steps in the unification of Italy in the correct order, earliest first.

options.text_md: Garibaldi's volunteers drive the Bourbon rulers out of southern Italy
Victor Emmanuel II is proclaimed king of united Italy
Mazzini founds Young Italy to work for a unitary Italian republic
Sardinia-Piedmont, allied with France, defeats Austria

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Young Italy was founded in 1831.
Step 2: Sardinia-Piedmont and France defeated Austria in 1859.
Step 3: Garibaldi's campaign in the south took place in 1860.
Step 4: Victor Emmanuel II was proclaimed king in 1861.
Step 5: So the order is c, d, a, b.

marking_scheme.step: Correct order c, d, a, b

questions.stem_md: Arrange these steps in the making of the British nation-state in chronological order.

options.text_md: The Act of Union joins England and Scotland
Ireland is forcibly incorporated into the United Kingdom
The English Parliament seizes power from the monarchy
Wolfe Tone and the United Irishmen lead a failed revolt

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Parliament seized power from the monarchy in 1688.
Step 2: Act of Union with Scotland, 1707.
Step 3: United Irishmen revolt, 1798.
Step 4: Ireland incorporated, 1801.
Step 5: So the order is c, a, d, b.

marking_scheme.step: Correct order c, a, d, b

questions.stem_md:
Map skills (practice). On an outline political map of Europe, locate and label:

**A.** The city where the Congress of 1815 met to redraw the map of Europe.

**B.** The city where elected representatives of the German states met as a parliament in 1848.

*(The CBSE board map list for History comes from "Nationalism in India"; this item builds the skill of reading a map of Europe.)*
questions.solution_md:
Step 1: The Congress met in Vienna, capital of Austria, on the river Danube.
Step 2: The 1848 parliament met in Frankfurt, on the river Main in western Germany.
Step 3: Mark each with a dot and write its name beside it.

marking_scheme.step: A: Vienna correctly located and labelled
B: Frankfurt correctly located and labelled

questions.stem_md:
Map skills (practice). On an outline political map of Europe, locate and label:

**A.** The capital city where revolutions broke out in July 1830 and again in February 1848.

**B.** The city where an uprising in 1830 led the Belgians to break away from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands.
questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Both French revolutions began in Paris, on the river Seine.
Step 2: The 1830 uprising that led to Belgian independence began in Brussels, north-east of Paris.
Step 3: Mark each with a dot and write its name beside it.

marking_scheme.step: A: Paris correctly located and labelled
B: Brussels correctly located and labelled

questions.stem_md: Mention any two measures taken by the French revolutionaries to create a sense of collective identity among the French people.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) Ideas of **la patrie** (the fatherland) and **le citoyen** (the citizen) stressed one community of equal citizens. (ii) A **new tricolour flag** replaced the royal standard, and the Estates General became the elected **National Assembly**.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Recall the measures: ideas of la patrie and le citoyen, the tricolour, the National Assembly, new hymns and oaths, a centralised administration with uniform laws, abolition of internal customs duties, uniform weights and measures, and French as the common language.
Step 2: Any two, each explained in a line, earn the marks.

questions.stem_md: How was a nation-state different from the dynastic empires of mid-eighteenth-century Europe? Give two points.

answer.model_answer_md: In a **nation-state**, most citizens share a **common identity and history**, and the people are sovereign. In a **dynastic empire**, such as the Habsburg Empire, **diverse peoples** speaking different languages were held together only by **loyalty to the ruler**.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Identify the basis of unity in each: shared identity (nation-state) vs allegiance to an emperor (dynastic empire).
Step 2: Use an example such as the Habsburg Empire, which included German, Magyar, Polish, Italian and Slav peoples.

marking_scheme.step: Dynastic empire: diverse peoples bound only by loyalty to the ruler

questions.stem_md: Why did the commercial middle classes of the German states want economic unification in the early nineteenth century? Give two reasons.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) Each of the 39 states had its **own currency, weights and measures**, which made trade slow and costly. (ii) **Customs barriers** raised prices. A unified market would let **goods and capital move freely**.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Recall the problem: a fragmented confederation with many currencies, measures and tariffs.
Step 2: Link it to the liberal demand for free movement of goods and capital, which the Zollverein (1834) partly met.

marking_scheme.step: Different currencies, weights and measures hampered trade
Customs barriers raised costs; wanted free movement of goods and capital

questions.stem_md: Give two ways in which language and folk culture were used by Romantics to build national feeling in Europe.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) German Romantics such as the **Grimm brothers collected old folk tales**, presenting them as the true voice of the nation. (ii) In Poland, **music and the Polish language** became symbols of resistance against Russian rule.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Romanticism valued emotion and the culture of ordinary people (Herder's *das volk*).
Step 2: Give one example of folk culture (folk tales, folk songs, dances) and one of language or music (Poland).

marking_scheme.step: Folk tales/songs collected as the nation's true spirit
Language/music used as a symbol of national resistance (Poland)

questions.stem_md: How did the July Revolution of 1830 in France affect other parts of Europe? Give two examples.

answer.model_answer_md: It inspired revolts elsewhere. (i) An **uprising in Brussels** led **Belgium to break away** from the United Kingdom of the Netherlands. (ii) Revolts broke out in parts of **Italy and Poland** (1831), though they were crushed.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: State what happened in France in July 1830.
Step 2: Give its effects elsewhere: Belgian independence and other uprisings (Italy, Poland in 1831).

marking_scheme.step: Effect on Belgium (break-away from the Netherlands)
A second effect, e.g. revolts in Italy or Poland, or spread of liberal ideas

questions.stem_md: What is an allegory? How did artists use allegory to represent a nation in the nineteenth century?

answer.model_answer_md: An **allegory** is a **person or a thing that stands for an abstract idea**, such as liberty. Artists showed nations as **female figures**, such as **Marianne for France** and **Germania for Germany**, with symbols showing what the nation stood for.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Define allegory.
Step 2: Apply it: female figures with symbols (red cap, tricolour, oak leaves, sword) made the abstract nation visible.

marking_scheme.step: Nation shown as a female figure with symbols, with an example

questions.stem_md: A student says: "Britain became a nation-state through one sudden revolution, just like France." Correct the student, giving two points.

answer.model_answer_md: The claim is wrong. (i) Britain formed through a **slow process spread over centuries**, not one upheaval. (ii) The **English** steadily extended their influence: the **Act of Union (1707)** brought in Scotland, and Ireland was **forcibly incorporated in 1801**.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Identify the error: "sudden revolution".
Step 2: Correct it with the nature of the process and two landmark steps.

marking_scheme.step: Long process, not a sudden revolution
English dominance with a landmark (1707 or 1801)

questions.stem_md: Why were the Balkan states fiercely jealous of one another in the late nineteenth century? Give two reasons.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) Each newly independent Balkan state used **history to claim that it once ruled more territory**, so their claims **overlapped**. (ii) Each hoped to **gain more land at the expense of others** as the Ottoman Empire retreated.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Link independence from the Ottomans to competing territorial claims.
Step 2: Note that each state wanted to expand into the same areas.

marking_scheme.step: Each wanted to expand at others' expense as Ottoman rule weakened

questions.stem_md: Describe any three changes Napoleon introduced to make administration more efficient in the territories under his control.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) The **Civil Code of 1804** ended privileges based on birth, gave **equality before the law** and secured the **right to property**. (ii) He **simplified administrative divisions** and **abolished the feudal system**, freeing peasants from serfdom and manorial dues. (iii) In towns he **removed guild restrictions** and **improved transport and communication**, which helped businessmen and small producers.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Choose three distinct reforms: legal (Civil Code), rural (end of feudalism), urban/economic (guilds, transport, uniform laws, weights and measures, common currency).
Step 2: Explain each in one line.

questions.stem_md: Explain three ways in which the conservative regimes set up after 1815 tried to stop the spread of liberal and nationalist ideas.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) The regimes were **autocratic**: they did not tolerate criticism or dissent. (ii) They **censored** the press, books and the stage to block ideas of liberty. (iii) They watched and **punished revolutionaries**: many, like Mazzini, were **sent into exile**, so activists had to work through **secret societies**.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Think of the tools of a conservative state: autocracy, censorship, repression.
Step 2: Give one consequence for revolutionaries (exile, secret societies).

questions.stem_md: "Hunger and hardship in the 1830s and 1840s prepared the ground for revolt in Europe." Support the statement with three points.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) **Population grew faster than jobs**, and many rural people migrated to overcrowded city slums. (ii) Small producers faced **competition from cheap machine-made goods**, especially textiles from England. (iii) **Bad harvests raised food prices**; in 1848 food shortages and unemployment brought Parisians onto the streets and the king fled.

questions.passage_md:
In 1825 a carter takes a wagon of linen cloth from a town in the north of the German lands to a fair in the south. On the way he crosses the borders of **six states**. At each border a customs post charges a duty, and in each state he must change his money into a different currency and have his cloth re-measured in the local ell (a unit of length). The cloth that cost 100 thalers at home sells at the fair for 140 thalers, but by then the carter has paid about 30 thalers in duties and exchange charges.

Ten years later, after most of these states have joined a customs union, the same journey has no customs posts at the inner borders, and a new railway line is being planned along part of the route.

children.stem_md: How much of the carter's gross margin of 40 thalers in 1825 was left after duties and exchange charges?
children.solution_md: Gross margin: 140 − 100 = 40 thalers. Subtract about 30 thalers of duties and charges: about 10 thalers remain.

children.stem_md: Name the customs union that the states in the case had joined by 1835.

answer.model_answer_md: The **Zollverein** (formed in 1834).

children.solution_md: The Zollverein was formed in 1834 at the initiative of Prussia.

children.stem_md: **Either** (i): Using the case, explain why the commercial middle classes supported economic unification.

answer.model_answer_md: In 1825 duties, currency exchange and different measures **ate up most of the trader's margin**. A single market **without customs barriers** and with fewer currencies would let **goods and capital move freely** and make trade profitable, which is what liberals demanded.

children.solution_md: Use the numbers to show the cost of fragmentation and link it to the liberal demand for free movement of goods and capital.

marking_scheme.step: Costs of fragmentation shown from the case
Link to the liberal demand for a unified market

alternatives.stem_md: **Or** (ii): How could the planned railway, together with the customs union, strengthen national feeling?

answer.model_answer_md: A railway network would **link distant regions** and **speed up trade and travel**. With one customs union, people across the states would share **economic interests**, which helped create the feeling of belonging to **one German nation**.

alternatives.solution_md: Link mobility and shared economic interest to a sense of national unity.

marking_scheme.step: Railways link regions and boost movement
Shared economic interests build national feeling

questions.stem_md: Which of the following was common to the unification of **both** Germany and Italy?

options.text_md: A leading state ruled by a monarchy, a skilful chief minister, and a war against Austria
An elected parliament that successfully wrote the national constitution
A popular uprising that abolished the monarchy
A decision of the Congress of Vienna to create the new nation

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Germany: Prussia (a monarchy) and its chief minister Bismarck; one of the three wars was against Austria (1866).
Step 2: Italy: Sardinia-Piedmont (a monarchy) and its chief minister Cavour; with France it defeated Austria (1859).
Step 3: So (a). (b) failed in Frankfurt in 1848; (c) did not happen, both new states were monarchies; (d) is false, the Vienna settlement kept both lands divided.

questions.stem_md: In an imagined German state with a liberal constitution in the 1830s, which of these people would most likely have had the right to vote?

options.text_md: A widow who owns a bakery
A landless farm labourer
A young woman working in a textile mill
A man who owns a printing press

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Liberals of this period usually limited the vote to **property-owning men**.
Step 2: The printing-press owner is a man with property, so (d).
Step 3: The widow owns property but is a woman, and women were excluded; the labourer and the mill worker own no property.

questions.stem_md: Give one similarity and one difference between the unification of Germany and that of Italy.

answer.model_answer_md: **Similarity:** both were led by a **monarchy-ruled state** (Prussia, Sardinia-Piedmont) with a **chief minister** (Bismarck, Cavour) and involved **war with Austria**. **Difference:** Italy also had a **volunteer campaign** under **Garibaldi**; Germany was united mainly by the **Prussian army and bureaucracy**.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Compare the leaders and methods.
Step 2: Accept other valid differences, e.g. Germany ended with a ceremony at Versailles after war with France, Italy with the proclamation of Victor Emmanuel II in 1861.

questions.stem_md: Imagine you are a teacher in Warsaw in the 1840s, when Russian has been forced on Polish schools. Based on what Poles actually did in this period, suggest two peaceful ways to keep national feeling alive.

answer.model_answer_md: (i) Keep using **Polish** at home, in church gatherings and in religious teaching, as the clergy did. (ii) Teach children **Polish music and folk dances** such as the **polonaise and mazurka**, which composers like Kurpinski had made national symbols.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Recall how Poles resisted: language (clergy using Polish) and culture (music, folk dances).
Step 2: Apply them to the teacher's situation.

marking_scheme.step: A way based on language, linked to Polish practice
A way based on music or folk culture, linked to Polish practice

questions.stem_md: Napoleon is described both as a destroyer of democracy and as a spreader of revolutionary principles. Which description do you find more convincing? Justify with three points.

answer.model_answer_md: Both are true, but for Europe he was **more a spreader of revolutionary principles**. (i) His **Civil Code** gave equality before the law and the right to property. (ii) He **ended feudalism** and guild restrictions. (iii) Yet he **ended democracy** in France and imposed **taxes, censorship and conscription**, so he spread reforms, not freedom.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Take a position.
Step 2: Support it with evidence from both sides.
Step 3: Accept the opposite position if it is backed by evidence (e.g. loss of political freedom, hostility in conquered lands).

marking_scheme.step: Evidence of loss of democracy/freedom weighed in the judgement

questions.stem_md: Was the formation of the United Kingdom of Great Britain equally beneficial to all the nations of the British Isles? Analyse with three points.

answer.model_answer_md: No. (i) The **English** gained most: their wealth, power and Parliament dominated the new state. (ii) **Scotland's** culture was suppressed: Highland Scots lost the use of Gaelic and their traditional dress, and many were expelled. (iii) **Ireland's** Catholic majority was dominated by Protestants backed by England; after the **1798** revolt it was **forcibly incorporated** in 1801.

questions.solution_md:
Step 1: Compare the experience of each nation.
Step 2: Conclude that the union served English dominance.
